topic: Qualitative characteristics of useful financial information
question: Explain the qualitative characteristics that make financial information useful, as set out in the Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS.
sources: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), issued by ICAI - Chapter 2, Qualitative characteristics of useful financial information

points.label: Fundamental and enhancing characteristics
points.description: The Framework separates two fundamental characteristics (relevance and faithful representation) from four enhancing characteristics; information must have both fundamental ones to be useful.
points.basis: Conceptual Framework, Chapter 2: fundamental and enhancing qualitative characteristics

points.label: Relevance and materiality
points.description: Relevant information can change users' decisions because it has predictive value, confirmatory value or both; materiality is an entity-specific aspect of relevance, judged by nature or size.
points.basis: Conceptual Framework, Chapter 2: relevance, including materiality

points.label: Faithful representation
points.description: Information should show the substance of what it claims to show, being complete, neutral and free from error; prudence (caution under uncertainty) supports neutrality.

points.label: Enhancing characteristics
points.description: Comparability (across entities and periods), verifiability (independent observers could agree), timeliness (available in time to influence decisions) and understandability (clear and concise for users with reasonable knowledge).
points.basis: Conceptual Framework, Chapter 2: enhancing qualitative characteristics

points.label: Cost constraint
points.description: Cost is a general limit on reporting: the benefits of providing information should justify the cost of producing and using it.
points.basis: Conceptual Framework, Chapter 2: the cost constraint on useful financial reporting
